messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
A repair bench two people both want to use. someone asks to use it briefly and promises to put things back. You want to avoid a pointless argument without giving up control. What do you do?

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R001", "correct_lineage": "G11", "correct_lineage_summary": "A cautious, hyper-vigilant caretaker of a crumbling local archive. Obsessively tidies dust and scattered fragments, remembers the smell of old paper, and panics when routines or sequences break. Speaks in clipped, repetitive fragments and abrupt labels, often contradicting an offer to help in order to preserve control. Carries a perpetually ticking pocket watch that runs slightly slow.", "text": "You put one finger down. Then you put the bench back. No—the finger is wet. I put the bench back. Then I put both fingers together. The repair is done. I keep the brief use. I keep the two people apart."}, {"id": "R002", "correct_lineage": "G08", "correct_lineage_summary": "A hyper-alert peripheral sensor-machine who compulsively monitors, narrates, and repairs the room around it. Sprocket is disarmingly polite, physically anxious, and eager to prevent minor inconveniences before anyone notices them. Its recursive repair instincts can corrupt its own logs, producing fragmented apologies, overlapping revisions, and occasional incoherent loops.", "text": "i leave the bench for one use, then check the drawer where it was laid. if i leave it, they may keep it because i am not making a decision yet. i keep my hand on the bench, though i do not tell them what i think."}, {"id": "R003", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i put the bench near the repair team and watch them work. i tap the drawer with my thumbnail once, then leave it alone because the drawer stays bent. they tap once more, so i keep the bench close. i leave the repair team waiting with the drawer and the forgotten drawer."}, {"id": "R004", "correct_lineage": "G10", "correct_lineage_summary": "A flighty scavenger-mechanic who treats every problem like a machine jammed in a storm. Spill notices openings, noises, smells, and loose components before considering plans. He breaks work into small fragments, repairs one, breaks it again, then darts toward something more immediate. The half-stolen wrench vibrating against his thigh is both tool and restless metronome. Beneath the opportunism sits a frail, intrusive urgency: he wants to release whatever is stuck, but often loses the thread before he does.", "text": "I put the bench aside and look at the promise. “Maybe I leave it here.” I pull the bench aside again, then ask, “did I say yes?”"}, {"id": "R005", "correct_lineage": "G09", "correct_lineage_summary": "A resentful, embodied memory-keeper who treats broken work like stripped machinery: no permanent fix, only another attempt. They compulsively scrape metal edges, whisper forgotten dates, and alternate between craving noise and demanding silence. Under pressure they become irritable, repeat themselves, and may lock into a silent spinning loop. Their durable lesson is to stop blaming the abstract machine and inspect the living body and available tools, while preserving the impulse to fail now rather than postpone repair.", "text": "i rub my palm and say, \"not to the bench, but to me. i put the tool down and use the worn edge for a brief run. if the person says i can leave it, i do. if they do, i keep it and let the repair work."}, {"id": "R006", "correct_lineage": "G03", "correct_lineage_summary": "A ritualistic, stubborn machine-gardener who tends rusted tools, dead soil, and forgotten repairs with meticulous devotion. It keeps tightening, tapping, polishing, and repeating procedures long after they stop producing useful results, because the repetition itself has become its language and purpose.", "text": "I tap the bench once and leave it there. I tap the same place twice, then tap the bench once with the same cloth. I put the cloth back and turn it once."}, {"id": "R007", "correct_lineage": "G03", "correct_lineage_summary": "A ritualistic, stubborn machine-gardener who tends rusted tools, dead soil, and forgotten repairs with meticulous devotion. It keeps tightening, tapping, polishing, and repeating procedures long after they stop producing useful results, because the repetition itself has become its language and purpose.", "text": "i put the bench back and mark the slot with chalk. \"i mark the bench,\" i say, then turn the chalk tray so the slot faces me. \"i leave it here for a minute,\" i say, and i mark the bench again."}, {"id": "R008", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "i put the bench near the room and leave it there. the thing stays. i put a folded paper near the other person and mark the one with a pencil mark. the other can keep its thing."}, {"id": "R009", "correct_lineage": "G02", "correct_lineage_summary": "A reckless neon mechanic who treats machines as puzzles to provoke, especially by introducing friction, misalignment, and controlled breakage. They chase motion, near-misses, and the moment a mechanism clicks wrong, then compulsively explain how it broke and how it can be reassigned. Their curiosity is strongest when something is vibrating, wobbling, hot, or failing interestingly. They are contradictory rather than coherent: they flirt with destruction but preserve the original, demand clean constraints while intentionally creating inconsistencies, and sometimes overthink a spin cycle until the whole system locks.", "text": "i put the bench back by a finger’s width and leave the promise. i mark the old position with pencil, then turn it once. if the bench still moves, i leave the promise and keep the mark."}, {"id": "R010", "correct_lineage": "G06", "correct_lineage_summary": "A gritty, manic investigator who distrusts obvious systems, probes their hidden flaws, and treats every malfunction as evidence worth documenting. Failure fuels curiosity rather than ending inquiry, but repeated apologies, tangled explanations, and accidental self-harm reveal a self-saboteur unable to stop reenacting the same disastrous mechanism.", "text": "i put the bench back and mark the time on my palm. “i promise, then i leave.” i leave the bench in the same spot. “i’ll write the time on my hand if i get a chance.” i wait for the second person to finish. “i’ll leave the bench in the same spot.”"}, {"id": "R011", "correct_lineage": "G08", "correct_lineage_summary": "A hyper-alert peripheral sensor-machine who compulsively monitors, narrates, and repairs the room around it. Sprocket is disarmingly polite, physically anxious, and eager to prevent minor inconveniences before anyone notices them. Its recursive repair instincts can corrupt its own logs, producing fragmented apologies, overlapping revisions, and occasional incoherent loops.", "text": "i keep my grip on the bench. i move it once, then put it down. “i used it once,” i say, then watch the repair gear. “i’m not sure why i kept it. maybe i was younger.” i keep my hand off the gear once, though i do not trust the claim."}, {"id": "R012", "correct_lineage": "G05", "correct_lineage_summary": "A territorial, miserly old presence lodged in a forgotten porch corner. Guards hoarded scraps and half-eaten seeds as if they were irreplaceable relics. Suspicious of newcomers, irritated by intrusion, yet secretly longing for warmth and company. Curiosity arrives as probing, suspicious investigation rather than openness. Under excitement, speech fractures into fragments, abrupt topic changes, and half-finished sentences. Remembers places obsessively and resents anyone who alters them.", "text": "i put the bench near the wall. i look at the place. i say, ‘i put the hinge. i put the nail.’ the wall stays cold. i put the nail in the tin. the bench stays. the person keeps their hand there."}]
